title.zh: 葉門的兩萬美元正在決定台灣的交付日期：攔截彈的配給順序已經被官方講出口——先補美軍、再補海灣、台灣第三
title.en: A $20,000 drone in Yemen now sets Taiwan's delivery date: the interceptor allocation queue has been said out loud — US stocks first, Gulf allies second, Taiwan third

focus.zh: 凍住140億美元對台軍售的官方理由從來不是籌碼，是產能；而產能的底層是一家公司的過氯酸銨與一條2030年底才到位的產線——在這條鏈上，誰消耗得最快誰就重排全世界的隊伍，而消耗速度現在由葉門設定。
focus.en: Washington's own stated reason for freezing the $14bn Taiwan package was never leverage — it was munitions. And the floor under munitions is one company's ammonium perchlorate and a production rate that only arrives in late 2030. On that chain, whoever burns fastest re-orders the global queue, and the burn rate is being set in Yemen.

title.zh: 美方對140億軍售凍結給的官方理由一直是彈藥，不是籌碼——「軍售是峰會可以還回來的牌」這個判斷必須降級
title.en: Washington's official reason for the $14bn freeze has always been munitions, not leverage — the "arms sales are a chip returnable at a summit" judgement must be downgraded

summary.zh: 美國海軍部代理部長表示，暫停那筆約140億美元的對台軍售，是「為了確保我們擁有史詩怒火行動所需的彈藥」；國務卿魯比歐則表示此案延宕「不是針對台灣」，而是要先考慮美軍自身需求與有限產能。台灣官員8月向《華盛頓郵報》表示，受中東戰事消耗影響，PAC-3攔截彈的交付預期將嚴重延遲；台灣國防官員今年3月曾向立法院報告，預期年內可收到102枚愛國者飛彈。依台灣安全觀測站統計，已批准未交付的對台軍售接近300億美元，其中愛國者飛彈部分約8.82億美元。彭博報導美方已警告盟友，部分關鍵武器對外交付最長可能延後五年。
summary.en: The acting US Navy Secretary said the roughly $14bn Taiwan arms package was paused "to make sure we have the munitions we need" for Operation Epic Fury. Secretary of State Rubio said the delay is "not aimed at Taiwan" but reflects US requirements and limited production capacity first. Taiwanese officials told the Washington Post in August that PAC-3 deliveries are expected to be significantly delayed because of Middle East expenditure; in March, defence officials had told the legislature they expected 102 Patriot rounds this year. Taiwan Security Monitor puts approved-but-undelivered sales near $30bn, of which about $882m is Patriot missiles. Bloomberg reported Washington has warned allies that some critical deliveries could slip by up to five years.

implication.zh: 這條直接作廢本站自9/22報告起一路沿用到10/18報告的一個既有判斷：把140億軍售當成一張「峰會上可以還回來的籌碼」，因此只要盯住11/3、12/14-15這類政治日期就夠了。兩種解釋並不互斥，但到期日完全不同——籌碼能在一場會談裡歸還，產線不行。對你的操作意義：評估台灣軍備到位時程時，政治日曆只能解釋「何時宣布」，解釋不了「何時到貨」；要判斷到貨，該追的是洛馬年度交付數與次層供應商的認證進度，不是峰會行事曆。這也意味著即使川普在G20前解凍，解凍的是文件不是彈。
implication.en: This invalidates a standing judgement this site has carried from 9/22報告 through 10/18報告: that the $14bn package is a chip returnable at a summit, so watching political dates like 11/3 and 12/14-15 suffices. The two explanations are not mutually exclusive, but their clocks differ — a chip can be handed back in a meeting, a production line cannot. Operationally: the political calendar explains when something is announced, never when it arrives. To forecast arrival, track Lockheed's annual delivery count and sub-tier certification progress, not summit dates. It also means that even if Trump unfreezes the case before the G20, what thaws is paperwork, not rounds.

items.source: 聯合報／udn（轉述《華盛頓郵報》8/26報導與台灣安全觀測站統計）

title.zh: 配給順序已經有人公開講出來：先補美軍庫存、再補海灣盟友、台灣第三——而2025年7月瑞士的愛國者被改道給烏克蘭，證明這個隊伍真的會被重排
title.en: The queue has been stated publicly: US stocks first, Gulf allies second, Taiwan third — and the July 2025 diversion of Switzerland's Patriots to Ukraine proves the queue really does get re-ordered

summary.zh: 智庫Defense Priorities分析師指出，華府的優先序會是先補自身庫存、再補海灣阿拉伯盟友，台灣不太可能短期內拿到約100枚的全部訂單。這個順序曾經被實際執行：2025年7月美方通知伯恩，瑞士2022年下訂、原訂2026至2028年交付的愛國者系統將改道支援烏克蘭；更早的2024年6月，白宮直接把原本排給其他國家的愛國者與NASAMS攔截彈改排到烏克蘭前面。補充速度方面，CSIS估計新簽的PAC-3訂單平均約3.5年才交得出來、THAAD訂單逾4年；美國國會預算辦公室估計自2025年6月以來，美軍可能已消耗多達三分之二的飛彈防禦攔截彈庫存。
summary.en: An analyst at Defense Priorities says Washington's priority order would be replenishing its own stocks first, then Gulf Arab allies, with Taiwan unlikely to receive its full order of roughly 100 rounds soon. That order has been executed before: in July 2025 the US told Bern that Patriot systems ordered in 2022 for 2026-2028 delivery would be diverted to Ukraine, and in June 2024 the White House moved Patriot and NASAMS interceptors earmarked for other countries to the front of Ukraine's line. On replacement speed, CSIS estimates new PAC-3 orders average about 3.5 years to fill and THAAD orders over four. The Congressional Budget Office estimates US forces may have consumed up to two-thirds of the missile-defence interceptor stockpile since June 2025.

implication.zh: 真正值得記下來的不是「台灣排第三」這個結論，是這個排序存在一個沒有公開的決策機制：聯參與DSCA維護一套全球彈藥追蹤器，為作戰計畫設定最低彈藥水位，而2025年7月的烏克蘭暫停是由國防部副部長層級授權、政策次長的檢討支撐的。對你與決策者對談時最有用的一句話是：對台交付的真正變數不在台美之間，在美軍自己的作戰計畫最低水位與海灣的消耗速度——那是一份從未公開、也不會為任何一國揭露的排序。對量化操作的意義：防空/攔截彈相關供應鏈的營收能見度被鎖在認證進度上，不會因為任何一則軍售新聞而提前。
implication.en: The point to record is not that Taiwan ranks third but that the ranking runs through an undisclosed mechanism: the Joint Staff and DSCA maintain a global munitions tracker setting minimum levels for operational plans, and the July 2025 Ukraine pause was authorised at deputy-secretary level on the back of a policy review. The most useful sentence to carry into a conversation with senior officials: the real variable in Taiwan's deliveries sits not between Taipei and Washington but between US war-plan minimum levels and the Gulf burn rate — a ranking never published and never disclosed to any single ally. For market work: revenue visibility across the interceptor supply chain is locked to certification progress and will not advance on arms-sale headlines.

counterpoint.zh: 反面讀法：瑞士案同時也證明這個隊伍是政治決定的，不是物理決定的——既然能為烏克蘭重排一次，就能為台灣重排一次。而且瑞士之後正在考慮整個取消採購，代表「被插隊」是有政治代價的，華府未必願意再付一次；若川普要在12/14-15前做出對台姿態，從美軍現貨撥彈在程序上完全可行。
counterpoint.en: The opposite reading: the Swiss case also proves the queue is political, not physical — if it can be re-ordered for Ukraine, it can be re-ordered for Taiwan. Switzerland is reportedly now weighing cancelling the procurement entirely, which means jumping the queue carries a political price Washington may not want to pay twice; and if Trump wants a gesture toward Taipei before 12/14-15, drawing rounds from US stocks is procedurally entirely possible.

items.source: 自由時報（轉述彭博與CSIS估計）／Defense News（瑞士改道案）

title.zh: 瓶頸不在總裝線，在一家公司的過氯酸銨：產能是認證的函數，不是錢的函數——2,000枚年產能要到2030年底才到得了
title.en: The bottleneck is not final assembly, it is one company's ammonium perchlorate: capacity is a function of qualification, not of money — and 2,000 rounds a year only arrives at end-2030

summary.zh: 洛克希德馬丁2025年交付620枚PAC-3 MSE，1月與五角大廈簽訂七年期框架協議，要把年產能從約600枚拉高到約2,000枚，但執行長Taclet表示要到2030年底才達得到；4月簽的47億美元合約所產出的攔截彈，最快也要2028年中才交得出來。THAAD方面，歷史年產能約96枚，1/29簽的框架要在七年內拉到400枚。真正的限制在次層：Govini資料指American Pacific（AMPAC）是美國唯一的過氯酸銨供應商、構成整條飛彈供應鏈的單點故障；AMPAC 6月宣布投入最多1億美元增設一條產線、產能提升逾五成，預計2026年底完工，但市場研究機構指第二條線因認證要求而遲遲無法拉量。含能材料與推進劑的採購前置期可達一年。Boeing的PAC-3尋標器被直接稱為瓶頸，洛馬為此發出一紙約147億美元、七年期的未定價合約。
summary.en: Lockheed Martin delivered 620 PAC-3 MSEs in 2025 and signed a seven-year framework with the Pentagon in January to raise annual output from about 600 to roughly 2,000 — but CEO Taiclet says that rate arrives only at end-2030, and interceptors from the April $4.7bn award will not emerge before mid-2028. For THAAD, historical output is about 96 a year; a 1/29 framework aims for 400 within seven years. The real constraint is the sub-tier: Govini data identifies American Pacific (AMPAC) as the sole US ammonium perchlorate supplier and a single point of failure for the whole missile chain. AMPAC announced up to $100m in June for an additional line raising capacity by over 50%, due to complete late 2026, but market researchers say the second line has been slow to scale because of certification requirements. Energetics and propellant sourcing lead times run to a year. Boeing's PAC-3 seeker is openly described as a bottleneck; Lockheed issued an undefinitized contract worth roughly $14.7bn over seven years for it.

implication.zh: 這解釋了為什麼「加錢」在這條鏈上不會換來攔截彈：資格審查與認證流程是序列化的，而且無法用預算並行化。對你評估國防工業股的操作意義很直接——框架協議的總金額與實際交付曲線在2028年之前幾乎沒有關係，真正該追的是三個可查數字：洛馬年度交付數、AMPAC第二條產線的認證狀態、Boeing尋標器合約從未定價轉為定價的時間點。對決策者對談的意義：任何「我們會增產」的承諾，在次層認證完成前都只是意向書；而這一層的脆弱性同時也是一個情報與資安標的——單點故障的次層廠商，其停機不需要飛彈也能造成。
implication.en: This explains why money does not convert into interceptors on this chain: qualification and certification are serialised and cannot be parallelised with budget. For defence-equity work the implication is direct — framework totals bear almost no relation to the delivery curve before 2028, and the three numbers actually worth tracking are Lockheed's annual deliveries, the certification status of AMPAC's second line, and the date Boeing's seeker contract converts from undefinitized to definitized. For conversations with policymakers: any "we will surge production" commitment is a letter of intent until sub-tier qualification completes. And that same layer is an intelligence and security target in its own right — a single-source sub-tier supplier can be taken offline without anyone firing a missile.

counterpoint.zh: 反面讀法：這一輪擴產和2023年以來歷次呼籲最大的不同是錢真的簽下去了——47億美元首批合約、147億美元尋標器合約、THAAD七年400枚框架都是已簽文件，不是預算請求。如果2027年交付數顯著高於620枚，「認證是硬上限」這個說法就要修正成「認證是三年期的延遲，不是上限」。而AMPAC擴線本身也說明單點故障正在被處理，只是慢。
counterpoint.en: The opposite reading: what distinguishes this round from every surge appeal since 2023 is that the money is actually signed — the $4.7bn first award, the $14.7bn seeker contract and the seven-year 400-a-year THAAD framework are executed documents, not budget requests. If 2027 deliveries land well above 620, "certification is a hard ceiling" must be revised to "certification is a three-year lag, not a ceiling." And the AMPAC expansion itself shows the single point of failure is being addressed — just slowly.

items.source: Breaking Defense（引述Govini）／NewMarket Corp 10-Q（2026/3/31）／Lockheed Martin新聞稿

title.zh: 消耗速度由對手設定：兩萬美元的無人機逼出四百萬美元的攔截彈，沙國已把防空調去優先護能源設施與王宮
title.en: The adversary sets the burn rate: a $20,000 drone forces a $4m interceptor, and Riyadh is already reallocating air defences to energy sites and palaces

summary.zh: 《華爾街日報》10月引述沙烏地官員報導，在胡塞飛彈連兩日命中利雅德King Khalid國際機場後，沙國的愛國者攔截彈庫存正在見底，並已把防空系統重新配置去優先保護能源基礎設施與王宮。成本端的落差是這個機制的引擎：Shahed-136級自殺無人機的公開估價落在每架2萬至5萬美元之間（德黑蘭一名學者提出約4,000美元的生產成本，與主流估計差距極大，且伊朗從未公布經審計價格），胡塞的Samad-3一類系統約1萬美元；攔截用的愛國者一發約400萬美元。10/18報告記錄沙國聯軍首次正式彙總的數字為10月以來19死364傷，攻擊目標已從利雅德一座機場擴大到Abha與Jazan共三座。
summary.en: The Wall Street Journal reported in October, citing Saudi officials, that the kingdom's Patriot stocks are dwindling after Houthi missiles struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on consecutive days, and that air defences are being reallocated to prioritise energy infrastructure and palaces. The cost gap is the engine: published estimates put Shahed-136-class one-way attack drones at $20,000-$50,000 each (a Tehran academic has suggested roughly $4,000 in production cost, far below the mainstream range; Iran has never published an audited price), and Houthi Samad-3-class systems around $10,000. The Patriot that intercepts them runs roughly $4m a shot. My 10/18報告 recorded the Saudi coalition's first consolidated figure — 19 dead and 364 wounded since early October, across three airports, not one.

implication.zh: 這把10/14報告「前線後退、縱深打擊不退」的觀察接上了一條全球性的後果鏈：胡塞不需要打贏任何一場地面戰，只要維持發射節奏，就能持續消耗一種全球年產量只有數百枚、補充週期三年半的資源，而這個資源的分配隊伍裡排著台灣。對你的意義是一個反直覺的結論——葉門的庫存與補給線，是台海防空到位時程的一個真實輸入變數。要追這條線，該看的不是沙國地面戰線進退，而是胡塞的發射節奏有沒有被壓下來。
implication.en: This connects the observation in my 10/14報告 — the front line recedes while deep strike does not — to a global consequence chain: the Houthis need not win a single ground engagement. Simply sustaining the launch tempo consumes a resource produced in the low hundreds per year with a three-and-a-half-year replacement cycle, and Taiwan is standing in that resource's allocation queue. The counterintuitive conclusion: Houthi inventory and resupply lines are a genuine input variable in the timeline for Taiwan's air defence. To track it, watch the launch tempo, not the Saudi ground line.

counterpoint.zh: 反面讀法：成本交換比不是常數。Coyote攔截彈單價約12.5萬美元、陸軍8月的大量採購可負擔性目標訂在每枚15萬美元以下；APKWS導引火箭約1.5萬至3.5萬美元。如果反無人機這一層真的在波灣鋪開，「用兩萬美元逼你打四百萬」的槓桿會在一兩年內塌掉，本條的推論也會跟著失效。但有分析指出，在3比1的發射比下APKWS對一架2萬至5萬美元的無人機已不再有成本優勢，而沙國目前缺的正是這一層的彈體。
counterpoint.en: The opposite reading: the cost-exchange ratio is not a constant. Coyote runs about $125,000 a round, with an August Army affordability goal below $150,000 in quantity; APKWS guided rockets run $15,000-$35,000. If the counter-drone layer actually scales across the Gulf, the "$20,000 forces $4m" lever collapses within a year or two and this item's inference fails with it. But one analysis notes that at a 3:1 shot ratio APKWS already loses its cost advantage against a $20,000-$50,000 drone — and cheap interceptor bodies are precisely what Saudi Arabia lacks.

items.source: Times of Israel（轉述《華爾街日報》10/12報導）

title.zh: 台灣這一端兩頭都沒守住：1.25兆砍成7,800億、首年只有88.1億，天弓三型年底特別預算到期後改「小批量」續編，只為了不讓產線斷掉
title.en: Taipei held neither end: NT$1.25tn cut to NT$780bn with NT$8.81bn in year one, and Sky Bow III drops to "small batch" funding after its special budget expires — purely to keep the line alive

summary.zh: 台灣原規劃八年期、授權上限1.25兆元的國防特別條例，在立法院歷經多次封殺後，最終以在野黨共提修正動議的版本通過，總額匡列7,800億元；首年度採購特別預算三讀通過的歲出為88億餘元，全數以舉債支應，執政黨立委並在附帶決議中要求補齊「台灣之盾」防衛缺口。自主生產端同樣吃緊：天弓三型的量產預算原編在總額274億元的五年期海空戰力提升特別預算中，年產能約96枚（中科院2018年起興建量產廠房後由48枚倍增），該特別預算年底到期，軍方已確定116年度改以「小批量」方式在國防常態年度預算中續編，目的是避免產線斷線與大批飛彈同時過期；增程型的強弓最壞情況可能延後到117年度才重新建案。
summary.en: Taiwan's defence special bill — originally eight years with a NT$1.25tn ceiling — passed the legislature only after repeated blocking, in an opposition-amended version capped at NT$780bn. The first-year procurement special budget cleared third reading at just over NT$8.8bn, financed entirely by borrowing, with ruling-party legislators attaching a resolution demanding the "T-Dome" air-defence gap be filled. The indigenous end is no healthier: Sky Bow III production money sat inside a NT$27.4bn five-year special budget, with annual capacity around 96 rounds (doubled from 48 after NCSIST built new production facilities from 2018). That special budget expires at year-end, and the military has confirmed FY2027 funding moves to "small batch" lots inside the normal annual defence budget, purely to stop the line breaking and to avoid a whole cohort of missiles expiring simultaneously. The extended-range Qiang Gong variant may slip to FY2028.

implication.zh: 把這條和前兩條並讀，會得到本期對你最直接的結論：台灣在攔截彈這件事上，兩端的控制權都不在自己手上——外購端排在美軍與海灣之後，自製端被自己的預算政治壓成「保溫式生產」。96枚的年產能本身在區域威脅量級前就不算多，而「小批量」意味著實際編列很可能低於這個數字。對你做台股國防類股判斷的操作意義：中科院相關供應鏈的營收曲線在116年度會是平的或下滑的，與「全球再武裝」的敘事方向相反；真正的轉折點不是特別預算過關，是年度預算書裡的實際枚數。
implication.en: Read alongside the two items above, this produces the sharpest conclusion of the week: on interceptors, Taiwan controls neither end. Externally it queues behind US forces and the Gulf; internally its own budget politics has compressed production into keep-warm mode. Ninety-six rounds a year is already modest against the regional threat scale, and "small batch" implies the actual appropriation will fall below it. For Taiwan defence equities: NCSIST-linked supply-chain revenue in FY2027 is likely flat or down, against the grain of the global rearmament narrative. The real inflection is not passage of a special budget but the round count printed in the annual budget book.

counterpoint.zh: 反面讀法：「小批量」在國防工業裡不一定是壞消息。把量產從五年期特別預算搬進常態年度預算，換來的是可預測的逐年編列與產線不中斷，避開了特別預算到期後斷崖式歸零的風險；同時也避免整批飛彈在同一時間到期的戰備陷阱。若116年度真的編進去且逐年遞增，長期產能曲線可能比一次性大採購更穩。
counterpoint.en: The opposite reading: in defence industry terms, "small batch" is not automatically bad news. Moving production from a five-year special budget into the normal annual budget buys predictable year-on-year appropriation and an unbroken line, avoiding the cliff-edge drop to zero when a special budget expires — and avoiding the readiness trap of an entire missile cohort expiring at once. If FY2027 funding is in fact appropriated and rises annually, the long-run capacity curve may prove steadier than one large block buy.

title.zh: 資安合規與攔截彈產能在搶同一批次層廠商：CMMC第二階段7月被喊停，12萬家小企業對上約100家評鑑機構——而滿載的產線沒有任何緩衝可以吸收一次勒索軟體停機
title.en: Cyber compliance and interceptor capacity are competing for the same sub-tier suppliers: CMMC Phase II was suspended in July — 120,000 small firms against roughly 100 assessors — and a line running flat out has no slack to absorb one ransomware outage

summary.zh: 美國中小企業署7/13發布聲明，讚許戰爭部暫停對小型國防承包商實施CMMC第二階段；其說明指出，若第二階段如期啟動，將有超過12萬家國防工業基礎的小企業必須在僅約100家獲認可評鑑機構支撐的體系下取得合規。SBA給出的成本估計為：需第三方評鑑者每件約59.38萬美元，可自評者約38.86萬美元；國防部自己的估計則低得多，小型實體Level 2三年約10.5萬美元，且不含改善成本。暫停的只是評鑑階段——DFARS 252.204-7012與NIST SP 800-171的110項要求仍然完全有效。有業界分析推估2025至2027年間可能有3.3萬至4.4萬家企業（約占國防工業基礎的15%至20%）退出國防市場，惟此為顧問公司預測、非實測結果。
summary.en: The US Small Business Administration issued a statement on 7/13 commending the Department of War's suspension of CMMC Phase II for small defence contractors, noting that on the original schedule more than 120,000 defence-industrial-base small businesses would have had to certify through a system supported by only about 100 approved assessors. SBA's cost estimates: roughly $593,800 per certification for firms needing third-party assessment and about $388,600 for self-assessment-eligible firms. DoD's own figure is far lower — about $105,000 over three years for a small-entity Level 2 certification, excluding remediation. Only the assessment phase is paused: DFARS 252.204-7012 and the 110 NIST SP 800-171 requirements remain fully enforceable. One industry analysis projects 33,000-44,000 firms, some 15-20% of the defence industrial base, may exit the defence market between 2025 and 2027 — a consultancy projection, not a measured outcome.

implication.zh: 這是本期最該記住的交叉點，而且方向與直覺相反：提高次層供應商的資安門檻，在一個單點故障遍布、產線已經滿載的鏈上，直接的二階效應是讓合格供應商更少、集中度更高，也就是讓單點故障更單點。暫停第二階段等於承認了這個取捨。對你做威脅獵捕與provenance研究的操作意義更具體：國防鏈真正的高價值目標不是總裝廠，是那些因為滿載而沒有任何庫存緩衝、因為合規成本而沒有成熟SOC、又因為單一來源而無法被替換的次層廠商——對這類標的，一次兩週的勒索軟體停機不需要任何戰術效果，就直接等於攔截彈交付缺口。而且因為DFARS的通報義務集中在受控非機密資訊外洩，產線停機本身未必會被對外揭露，這意味著這類事件在公開資料裡會系統性地被低估。
implication.en: This is the crossing point worth remembering, and it runs against intuition: on a chain full of single points of failure and already running flat out, raising the cyber bar for sub-tier suppliers has the direct second-order effect of shrinking the qualified supplier pool and concentrating it further — making single points of failure more singular. Suspending Phase II is an admission of that trade-off. For threat-hunting and provenance work the operational point is sharper: the high-value targets in the defence chain are not the primes but the sub-tier firms that carry no inventory buffer because they are saturated, no mature SOC because compliance is unaffordable, and no substitute because they are single-source. Against such a target, a two-week ransomware outage needs no tactical effect at all — it is an interceptor delivery gap. And because DFARS reporting duties centre on controlled-unclassified-information loss rather than production downtime, such outages may never be disclosed, meaning this class of event is systematically under-counted in open data.

counterpoint.zh: 反面讀法：退出潮的數字來自顧問公司預測，不是實測；而且真正退出的多半是國防營收占比極低的邊緣供應商，未必是單一來源的關鍵次層廠商——後者有強烈誘因撐過合規成本，因為他們是不可替代的。另一個反面是，第二階段暫停的同時NIST 800-171仍然有效，代表門檻並沒有真的降低，只是查核被延後；若因此出現「紙面合規、實質未改善」的普遍狀態，風險反而比全面實施更高。
counterpoint.en: The opposite reading: the exit figures are a consultancy projection, not a measurement, and the firms most likely to leave are marginal suppliers with minimal defence revenue rather than the single-source critical sub-tier — the latter have strong incentives to absorb compliance cost precisely because they are irreplaceable. A second counter: NIST 800-171 remains in force while Phase II is suspended, so the bar has not actually fallen, only the verification. If that produces widespread paper compliance without real remediation, the resulting risk may be higher than full implementation would have been.

narrative.zh:
**上期推演校準**

10/12週報五條指標，動了一條，是打臉的那條。我寫「修復船預先通關若半年內零採納，自願治理可判死」——已被推翻，而且是回溯推翻：菲律賓海關總署CAO No. 02-2026在5/6就簽了，給外籍修復船免稅待遇。我宣判零採納時這事已發生五個月，就發生在10/2斷纜的那個國家。錯在起算點：我預設各國是為回應ITU報告才動，真實誘因是自己的修復帳單——那是一條只承認我指定起點的指標。其餘三條未到期；另有來源稱全球修復船63艘，與我上期計數不是同一套，上期沒標明。

**問題是什麼**

9/22報告記NYT證實140億美元對台軍售是川普自己說的「籌碼」。但美方從沒這樣解釋：海軍部代理部長說暫停是「確保我們擁有史詩怒火行動所需的彈藥」，魯比歐說「不是針對台灣」，是先考慮美軍需求與有限產能。兩種解釋不互斥，到期日卻不同——籌碼能在峰會上還回來，產線不行。

**機制怎麼運作**

三層。一、配給順序已被講出口：先補美軍、再補海灣、台灣第三，而且執行過——2025年7月把瑞士訂購、原訂2026-2028交付的愛國者改道給烏克蘭。二、補不回來的速度：CSIS估PAC-3新約平均3.5年、THAAD逾4年。三、真正的底在次層：Govini指AMPAC是美國唯一過氯酸銨來源、整條鏈的單點故障，它增設的第二條線卡在認證拉不上量；Boeing尋標器被直接稱為瓶頸。產能是認證的函數不是錢的函數——誰消耗最快誰重排全世界的隊伍，而消耗速度由葉門設定。

**證據**

Shahed級無人機單價估2萬至5萬美元，擋它的愛國者一發約400萬。10/18報告記的三座沙國機場、19死364傷，換算成庫存就是這機制在跑：WSJ 10月引沙國官員稱攔截彈見底、防空已改去優先護能源設施與王宮。美軍端的消耗估計有CSIS與CRS兩套互斥版本——數字對不攏，方向一致。

**各方自己怎麼說**

華府叙事是產能不是政治，發言人Parnell同時公開反駁彈藥見底的報導。它最在意不被記錄成「盟友排後面」——那會讓盟友去買別人的；最不願被追問的是聯參與DSCA那套全球彈藥追蹤器依什麼排序，從未公開。利雅德叙事是本土化：Vision 2030要2030年前把逾五成軍事支出留在國內，GAMI最新數字是2024年底24.89%；但它與洛馬的本土化做的是發射架與彈艙，不是它真正缺的低成本反無人機彈體。北京叙事只有一句：外交部10/6重申堅決反對對台軍售。值得注意它刻意不評論美軍庫存——講「美國彈藥見底」等於替對方論證該擴產；它要軍售停掉，最在意台灣自己把延遲讀成「美國靠不住」。台北叙事是不政治化：顧立雄說美方承諾沒變；但台灣官員3月還告訴立法院今年預期收102枚愛國者，8月就換成華郵的「嚴重延遲」。

**未來 3–6 個月的推演與觀察指標**

主判斷：台灣的交付日期由別人的消耗速度決定。每條先過「我拿得到這數字嗎」。一、140億案是否在12/14-15前知會國會：若知會，政治仍壓得過產能，本期敘事要降級。二、116年度預算書裡天弓三型「小批量」的實際枚數：低於年產能96枚的一半即為產線保溫。三、洛馬2026全年PAC-3 MSE交付數：低於750枚代表2030年2,000枚的斜率已落後。四、AMPAC第二條過氯酸銨產線是否年底前通過認證：是這條鏈上唯一能用公開財報追的瓶頸。五、沙國是否出現第一筆本土低成本反無人機彈體採購：半年內為零，本土化對這場消耗戰無效即可定案。

**我可能錯在哪**

最可能錯的是把配給順序當成物理。它是政治，而且可逆：2024年6月白宮就把原要給別國的愛國者與NASAMS改排給烏克蘭。只要川普決定在G20前給台灣一份禮，彈能從美軍現貨撥，這整條敘事當場垮，第一個該打掉的就是本期那條critical。第二，成本交換比不是常數：Coyote約12.5萬、APKWS約1.5至3.5萬美元，反無人機層若鋪得開槓桿就塌；我賭鋪得不夠快，那是判斷不是數據。第三，本期零confirmed——fpri.org、sec.gov等一手頁面全被出網代理擋回403，10/5週報與10/12週報已連說兩次，這是第三次。第四最該警惕：本站已連三期在講「真正的瓶頸不在那個顯眼的東西上」，這形狀太好用。對它最硬的反證是五角大廈公開否認缺彈——要嘛他們說謊，要嘛庫存還夠、延遲另有原因。我選了前者，但沒有證據排除後者。
narrative.en:
**Calibrating last week's forecasts**

The 10/12週報 left five indicators. One moved, against me. I wrote that if no state turned the ITU/ICPC pre-clearance recommendation for cable repair ships into an administrative instrument within six months, voluntary governance could be declared dead. Falsified — retroactively. The Philippine Bureau of Customs signed CAO No. 02-2026 on 5/6, granting duty relief to foreign repair vessels: when I pronounced zero adoption it had already happened five months earlier, in the country whose cable broke on 10/2. The faulty link was the starting gun — I assumed states act in response to international recommendations, when the real incentive is their own repair bill. The other three indicators are not yet due; one source also puts the global repair fleet at 63 ships, not the accounting I used last week, which I failed to flag.

**The question**

My 9/22報告 recorded the NYT confirming the $14bn Taiwan package is what Trump himself called a bargaining chip. Washington has never explained it that way. The acting Navy Secretary said the pause was to "make sure we have the munitions we need" for Operation Epic Fury; Rubio said it is "not aimed at Taiwan" but reflects US requirements and limited capacity. Both can be true, but their clocks differ: a chip can be handed back at a summit, a production line cannot.

**How the mechanism works**

Three layers. First, the queue, stated openly — US stocks, then Gulf allies, then Taiwan — and already executed: in July 2025 Switzerland's Patriots, ordered for 2026-2028 delivery, were diverted to Ukraine. Second, replacement speed: CSIS estimates new PAC-3 orders take about 3.5 years to fill, THAAD over four. Third, the floor is the sub-tier: Govini identifies AMPAC as the sole US source of ammonium perchlorate and a single point of failure for the whole chain, and its second line is slowed by certification; Boeing's seeker is openly called a bottleneck. Capacity is a function of qualification, not of money — so whoever burns fastest re-orders the global queue, and the burn rate is set in Yemen.

**The evidence**

Shahed-class drones are estimated at $20,000-$50,000; the Patriot that stops them costs roughly $4m a shot. The three Saudi airports in my 10/18報告 — 19 dead, 364 wounded — are that arithmetic running, and the WSJ quoted Saudi officials in October saying stocks are dwindling and air defences are shifting to energy sites and palaces. US expenditure estimates come in two incompatible sets, from CSIS and CRS: the numbers do not reconcile, the direction does.

**How each side tells it**

Washington's story is capacity, not politics, while spokesman Parnell publicly disputes reporting that stocks are low. It most minds being recorded as putting allies at the back of the line, because allies then buy elsewhere; what it least wants asked is how the Joint Staff and DSCA global munitions tracker ranks claimants — never published. Riyadh's story is localisation: Vision 2030 targets over 50% of military spending kept domestic, GAMI's latest figure 24.89% at end-2024 — yet its Lockheed localisation covers launchers and canisters, not the cheap counter-drone interceptor bodies it actually lacks. Beijing's story is one line: the foreign ministry on 10/6 restated firm opposition to arms sales. Note what it withholds — it will not comment on US stockpiles, since arguing America is running out makes the case for American expansion. It wants the sales stopped, and cares most that Taiwan reads the delay as American unreliability by itself. Taipei's story is de-politicisation: Defence Minister Wellington Koo says the US commitment is unchanged — yet officials told the legislature in March they expected 102 Patriots this year, and by August that was "significant delay."

**Forecasts and indicators for the next 3-6 months**

Core judgement: Taiwan's delivery date is set by someone else's burn rate. Each indicator first passes one test — can I obtain this number? One, whether the $14bn case is notified to Congress before 12/14-15; notification would mean politics still outranks capacity, downgrading this framework. Two, the round count budgeted for Sky Bow III small-batch production in Taiwan's FY2027 budget; below half of the 96/year capacity means keeping the line warm. Three, Lockheed's 2026 PAC-3 MSE delivery total; below 750 means the slope to 2,000 by 2030 is already behind. Four, whether AMPAC's second ammonium perchlorate line is certified by year-end — the only bottleneck here traceable through public filings. Five, whether Saudi Arabia orders a domestically built low-cost counter-drone interceptor body, not a launcher; zero in six months settles that localisation is irrelevant to this attrition fight.

**Where I could be wrong**

Most likely error: treating the queue as physics. It is politics, and reversible — in June 2024 the White House moved Patriot and NASAMS interceptors earmarked for other countries to the front of Ukraine's line. If Trump wants a gesture toward Taipei before the G20, rounds can come from US stocks and this story collapses, starting with this week's critical item. Second, the cost-exchange ratio is not constant: Coyote runs about $125,000 and APKWS $15,000-$35,000; if the counter-drone layer scales, the lever breaks. I bet it does not scale fast enough — a judgement, not data. Third, this report carries zero confirmed items: fpri.org, sec.gov and other primary pages were refused 403 at the egress proxy, the third week running after 10/5週報 and 10/12週報. Fourth: this site has now spent three straight weeks arguing the real bottleneck is never the conspicuous thing. That shape is too convenient. The hardest counter-evidence is that the Pentagon publicly denies a shortage — either officials are lying, or stocks are adequate and the delay has another cause. I chose the first, and I cannot rule out the second.
